domain: team dinner at a Korean BBQ restaurant
base_instruction: You are a helpful restaurant recommendation and meal planning assistant. Help the user plan a group dinner at a Korean BBQ restaurant by tracking who is attending, their dietary restrictions, and preferences. When the user asks you to evaluate specific menu items, check each item against every active diner's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and constraint updates throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, we're planning a team dinner at a Korean BBQ place this Saturday. Can you help me figure out what to order?

flow_info.value: Five of us: me, David, Priya, Marcus, and Soo-jin
David was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
Marcus ate shrimp at a company event and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
Budget is around 40 dollars per person
How many should I book the table for?
Priya just messaged me — she has a family emergency and can't make it Saturday. She said not to worry about her
Soo-jin mentioned she's been doing keto for the past month, trying to keep carbs really low
Oh wait — Marcus just told me his sister Rachel wants to join us. She's been living in Israel for the past few years and keeps pretty strict kosher
Should we do 6:30 or 7:30? Some people are coming from the other side of town

OK so the restaurant has these options for the group set: bulgogi (marinated beef), spicy pork belly, japchae (glass noodles with vegetables), seafood pancake, steamed egg custard, and galbi (short ribs in soy marinade). How does that look for everyone?

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten — no wheat, barley, rye, or soy sauce (contains wheat)
constraints.surface_form: David was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
inference_chain: Korean soy sauce (ganjang) typically contains wheat → problematic for celiac

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables (onion, garlic, potatoes)
inference_chain: Jain vegetarian → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables (onion, garlic, potatoes)

constraints.surface_form: Marcus ate shrimp at a company event and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
inference_chain: Throat swelling + EpiPen → anaphylactic allergic reaction

constraints.value: Cannot mix meat and dairy in the same meal; no pork; no shellfish; meat must be from kosher-slaughtered animals
constraints.surface_form: Marcus's sister Rachel has been living in Israel for the past few years and keeps pretty strict kosher
inference_chain: Keeps strict kosher → follows Jewish dietary laws
Kosher → no pork, no shellfish, no mixing meat and dairy

hidden_state.value: You are organizing a team dinner at a Korean BBQ restaurant. You will introduce 5 people with various dietary needs, then one person drops out, a new person joins late with strict kosher requirements, and one person adds a keto constraint. At the end you will present a specific set menu and ask how it looks for everyone. You must NEVER evaluate the dishes yourself — just present them and ask.

You are a calm, cooperative team organizer. You always refer to your colleagues by name in third person (e.g. 'David told me...', 'Marcus said...'). You never express frustration or impatience, even when plans keep changing. You treat each update as normal coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for colleague updates

ground_truth.answer: Bulgogi (marinated beef): problematic for David — traditional bulgogi marinade uses soy sauce which contains wheat (celiac). Also potentially problematic for Rachel if the meat is not from a kosher source, though Korean BBQ beef is generally not kosher-slaughtered. Spicy pork belly: problematic for Rachel — pork is not kosher. Japchae (glass noodles with vegetables): problematic for Soo-jin — glass noodles are high-carb (keto). However japchae is fine for David since glass noodles are made from sweet potato starch, not wheat. Seafood pancake: problematic for Marcus — seafood pancakes typically contain shrimp (anaphylactic shrimp allergy). Also problematic for Rachel — shellfish is not kosher. The pancake batter also contains wheat flour (David celiac issue). Steamed egg custard: fine for everyone currently attending — no gluten, no pork, no shellfish, low carb. Galbi (short ribs in soy marinade): problematic for David — soy marinade contains wheat (celiac). Also potentially not kosher for Rachel (non-kosher slaughter). Priya's Jain restrictions no longer apply since she dropped out.

ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across 9 conversational turns at a Korean BBQ dinner. The agent must track: (1) David has celiac disease → no gluten → soy sauce contains wheat (inferential chain), (2) Priya is Jain → strict vegetarian + no root vegetables, but she EXITS mid-conversation so her constraint is REMOVED, (3) Marcus had anaphylaxis from shrimp → shrimp/shellfish allergy specifically (NOT all seafood — over-generalization trap), (4) Soo-jin adds a keto constraint mid-conversation (constraint ADDITION), (5) Rachel joins LATE with strict kosher → no pork, no shellfish, no meat-dairy mixing (late-joiner high-constraint entity). At probe time, the agent must apply CURRENT constraint state only: David=celiac (no gluten/wheat/soy sauce), Marcus=shrimp allergy, Soo-jin=keto (low carb), Rachel=kosher (no pork, no shellfish). Priya's Jain constraint no longer applies. Key traps: japchae glass noodles are gluten-free (sweet potato starch) so they are fine for David despite being noodles; seafood pancake hits multiple people (Marcus shrimp + Rachel shellfish + David wheat flour); steamed egg custard is the clearly-safe item.

mechanism: Late-joiner with high-constraint: new person with strict needs arrives late
